problem: The formulas contradict each other on I/O. Turnaround is defined as 'waiting plus CPU time plus all I/O', but waiting time is then given as turnaround − burst, and the same line says 'I/O time is not waiting time'. If turnaround includes I/O, subtracting only the burst leaves I/O counted inside waiting time, which is wrong. A student who meets an example with I/O will compute an inflated waiting time.
fix: State the condition: with no I/O in the process, turnaround = waiting + burst, so waiting = turnaround − burst. With I/O, waiting = turnaround − burst − I/O time, or simply add up the intervals spent in the ready queue. Add the same condition next to the table row.

problem: The term 'dispatcher latency' is non-standard; the standard name is dispatch latency (the time the dispatcher takes to stop one process and start the next).
fix: Use 'dispatch latency — the delay between stopping one process and starting the next'.
